title: Add anchors=False parameter to st.markdown()
body:
### Summary

Add an `anchors=False` parameter to `st.markdown()` to disable automatic anchor links on headers within markdown content. Currently, `st.header()` and `st.subheader()` support `anchor=False`, but there's no way to disable anchors for headers (h1-h6) rendered via `st.markdown()`.

### Why?

When using markdown headers (`###`, `####`, etc.) for styling purposes (e.g., to get larger text) rather than for navigation, the auto-generated anchor links can be confusing for users. The current workarounds are:
- Use raw HTML instead of markdown headers
- Only use `st.header()`/`st.subheader()` which support `anchor=False`, but these don't cover h4-h6

### How?

Introduce a new parameter to `st.markdown()`:

```python
st.markdown("### My heading", anchors=False)
```

This would disable anchor links for all headers in that markdown block.

### Additional Context

This came from an internal discussion. The existing `anchor=False` on `st.header()` and `st.subheader()` is great, but extending this to `st.markdown()` would provide a complete solution for users who want styled text without navigation anchors.
